name: Digital Lending — Approved Partner Structural Check
sourceDocument: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
referenceNumber: not independently confirmed — RBI's notification PDF is CAPTCHA-gated and could not be fetched directly during this research pass
section: Para 17 (source provision; the registry rule is an internal-governance derivation)
confidenceNote: This is a mechanism change, not a renumbering. The September 2022 Guidelines' Para 8 required LSPs to be drawn from a 'board-approved list' maintained internally by the RE. The 2025 Directions instead require REs to report all deployed Digital Lending Apps (DLAs) — their own and their LSPs' — to RBI's Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) portal, keep the list current as engagements change, and have the Chief Compliance Officer or a board-designated official certify the data's accuracy. This provision took effect June 15, 2025. The approved-partners registry is this project's conservative internal pre-release control derived from that record-keeping/certification obligation; it is not a claim that Para 17 literally mandates this exact registry or proves CIMS compliance. Verify the primary RBI notice before using the paragraph citation externally.
clauseText: Regulated Entities shall report details of all Digital Lending Apps deployed by themselves or their Lending Service Providers through the RBI's Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) portal, and shall ensure this list is kept current and its accuracy certified by the Chief Compliance Officer or a board-designated official. RBI publishes the resulting list on its website, sourced from RE-submitted data without independent RBI validation, for the limited purpose of allowing customers to verify a DLA's claimed association with an RE.
observableGraphCondition: Any Actor with type=FINANCING_PROVIDER in the full proposedGraph whose actorId is not present in .regulatory/approved-partners.json.
implementationNotes: This check is NOT a verification that CIMS reporting has actually occurred, and it is NOT a legal RE-LSP contract check. It is a structural internal-governance gate: RBI's CIMS-certification obligation requires an RE to maintain an accurate internal record of active financing partners in the first place, in order to certify that record's accuracy to RBI. This check enforces that a new financing actor is tracked in the internal record (approved-partners.json) before it reaches production, which is a necessary precondition for correct CIMS certification, not a replication of the CIMS mechanism itself.
The check is performed against the FULL proposedGraph (not just the delta) to catch actors that were silently added in a prior un-reviewed change and only gain new activity in the current PR.
Adding a partner to approved-partners.json is an explicit compliance team action — it should not be automated or auto-approved.
The approved-partners.json file must be version-controlled and require separate approval to modify.
